clue.text: Move very fast to limit fire damage to outside

definitions.meaning: to drive or ride at great speed, a colloquial sense of the word
to burn only the surface of something, leaving the inside unharmed

explanation.surface: Firefighters rush in to keep a blaze from spreading beyond the outer walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to race along at speed, and to singe a surface with heat.

clue.text: Social problem out of control in parts of Central America

indicators.note: letters running out of control are thrown into a new order
the central letters of the next word are taken, dropping its outer pair of letters at each end

explanation.surface: A commentator laments disorder spreading through parts of Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central' picks MERIC, the five middle letters of AMERICA; 'out of control' rearranges them. 'in parts of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawbreaking is the classic example of a social ill that governments try to tackle.

clue.text: Engineers, despite being on time, went back to drawing board

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British Army
despite means though, as in 'though it rained'

explanation.surface: Engineers scrapped their plans even though they were running on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'being on' just places the last piece below the others.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back to the drawing board is an idiom for reconsidering a plan from scratch.

clue.text: Solitary type at home in Russian museum?

definitions.text: Solitary type at home in Russian museum?

parts.words: Solitary type at home in Russian museum?
parts.note: the great St Petersburg museum bears the name for a recluse's dwelling, so a loner would be at home there

explanation.surface: A loner feels most comfortable wandering a St Petersburg gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse living alone is the solitary type; the famous museum's name means his dwelling.

clue.text: Place to rest by river for sleepy little creature

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a room for sleeping
the Ouse is a river in England, a common crossword river

explanation.surface: A tired animal finds a riverside spot to take a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: The small rodent is famous for hibernating and dozing, as in Alice in Wonderland.

clue.text: Show lack of class and lack aspiration, so to speak

definitions.meaning: failing to sound the H at the start of words is a stereotyped mark of lower-class speech in Britain
aspiration is the breathy sound of an H, so leaving it out means lacking aspiration in the phonetic sense

explanation.surface: Someone is criticised for being common and having no ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'ouse' for 'house' is the British stereotype of a speaker with no class.

clue.text: Time before or after work for a jam session?

definitions.text: Time before or after work for a jam session?

parts.words: Time before or after work for a jam session?
parts.note: a jam session sounds like music, but here the jam is a traffic jam at the busy commuting period

explanation.surface: Musicians meet before or after their day jobs to play together.
explanation.definitionFit: The commuting peak when traffic is congested comes just before and after the working day.

clue.text: Sort out common law partner

definitions.meaning: to arrange or put things into sequence
the word that commonly partners 'law' in the phrase 'law and ...'

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to settle matters with a spouse they never formally married.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange is a verb sense; and 'law and' a familiar pairing completes the phrase with this word.

clue.text: Historically, part of house not yet full

definitions.meaning: in old country houses, a room for distilling and storing preserves and cordials
read as two words, 'there is still space', so the place is not full

explanation.surface: A guide explains that a part of the stately home still has space left.
explanation.definitionFit: A distilling room in a large house was a feature of earlier centuries, hence 'historically'.

clue.text: Very nasty coverage of politician endlessly winning

indicators.note: coverage of means the first word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: vicious means very nasty or savage

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A politician complains of savage press coverage that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very nasty' reads as describing the coverage, but it is the outer word; 'endlessly' drops the politician's last letter before 'coverage of' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being triumphant in a contest is a synonym for winning.

clue.text: It could be said to provide support for speaker

definitions.text: It could be said to provide support for speaker

parts.words: It could be said to provide support for speaker
parts.note: the speaker is someone giving a talk, and the raised platform holds them up

explanation.surface: A remark could be taken as backing for a person giving a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support for speaker' sounds like agreeing with a speaker, but it is literal: the thing the speaker stands on.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform at the end of a hall is where a lecturer stands to speak.

clue.text: Chief's war-cry

parts.note: the Apache leader's name, later shouted by paratroopers as they jumped

explanation.surface: A tribal leader's battle shout.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache chief's name became a famous yell used when leaping into action.

clue.text: Novelist inserting extra line? That's unlikely!

indicators.note: inserting means the novelist's name takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: Thomas Hardy was an English novelist
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Would a novelist really add one more line to his text? Doubtful!
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation, the word scoffs that something is scarcely likely.

clue.text: Hunted animal's leg cut

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened by losing its final letter

parts.note: a stage is a leg of a journey or race

explanation.surface: The hunted deer has an injured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' looks like the animal's limb but means a stretch of a journey; 'cut' removes its last letter. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is the classic quarry of the hunt.

clue.text: What's found in non sequitur is absurd — it's a gem!

indicators.note: an absurd arrangement signals that the letters are jumbled
what is found in a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: An illogical remark is ridiculous, but someone praises it as a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of NON is O; 'is absurd' rearranges O with SEQUITUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue-green stone is a semi-precious gem.

clue.text: Old coin cast in European gold for master, say

indicators.note: cast in means the coin is put inside the other letters

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a ducat was a gold coin used in Europe

explanation.surface: An antique coin is set into a European gold piece for a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is an example of a teacher, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Drinks available from Arabs in the souk

indicators.note: available from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Liquor can be bought from Arab traders in a market.
explanation.definitionFit: The anise-flavoured green spirits are strong alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Elegant as someone arriving on Tuesday

definitions.meaning: moving or looking stylish and refined
the nursery rhyme says 'Tuesday's child is full of grace', so a baby born on Tuesday is like this

explanation.surface: A stylish guest shows up on Tuesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Poised and refined are synonyms; the rhyme gives the Tuesday-born child this quality.

clue.text: Strangely erratic about one's standards

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the next piece
strangely means the letters of the next word are oddly reordered

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone's personal standards are oddly inconsistent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' turns ERRATIC into CRITERA; 'about' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Benchmarks for judging are standards; the word is the plural of criterion.

clue.text: Problem with ring for this style of wrestling

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A ring causes trouble for a certain wrestling style.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese form of wrestling between heavyweights is fought in a ring.

clue.text: Make rapid progress in life's work

definitions.meaning: a profession or occupation pursued through one's life

explanation.surface: Someone advances quickly in their chosen profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurtling along is the verb sense; a lifelong profession is the noun sense.

clue.text: Disease associated with plants I caught from the countryside

parts.note: rust is a fungal disease of plants
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A gardener admits catching a plant disease out in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural, of the country, is a synonym; the word describes country life.

clue.text: King's finally left to collect a subject

indicators.note: finally left means a letter departs from the end

parts.note: to pick is to collect, as fruit is picked
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: The monarch eventually leaves to gather a subject of his realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' and 'subject' suggest a realm, but the king is just K, and 'finally left' takes it off the end of TOPICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme for discussion is a subject or topic of talk.

clue.text: Special shoes required to get the best out of racehorses

definitions.meaning: sports shoes, called sneakers in the US

definitions.text: required to get the best out of racehorses
definitions.meaning: the people who train racehorses to peak form

explanation.surface: Particular footwear is needed to get top performance from racing horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic shoes and horse coaches are the two senses of the plural noun.

clue.text: As a rule, it may be said to be right

indicators.note: it may be said signals that a word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the idiom 'right as rain' means perfectly fine, so 'as a ... to be right' points to the wet weather word

explanation.surface: Someone claims that, as a rule, it is considered correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a' and 'to be right' together recall the British idiom 'right as rain'; that weather word, spoken, gives the monarch's period of rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign's period of ruling, or the act of ruling, is a synonym of rule.

clue.text: Spineless man's wife and child behaving badly

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A weak husband is pushed around by his wife and their unruly child.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A weakling with no backbone is a feeble, timid person.

clue.text: In which one can express warmth of unusually fine hearth

definitions.text: In which one can express warmth

indicators.note: unusually means the following letters are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A remarkably fine fireplace lets you show your warm feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: The temperature scale is a system in which degrees of heat can be stated.

clue.text: Labour performer -he dominates over Conservative

indicators.note: over means the ruling letters lie across the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to rule is to dominate

explanation.surface: A Labour politician dominates his Conservative rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour suggests the political party, but this is the Greek hero who performed twelve labours.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical strongman carried out the Twelve Labours, so he performed labours.

clue.text: As leader of rebellion, I celebrate this?

definitions.text: As leader of rebellion, I celebrate this?

indicators.note: leader of picks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: A rebel leader wonders whether he should hymn the revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a rebellion, and the whole clue describes a rebel leader praising one.
